This report records what one round explored and what it concluded. Where a direction was chosen, that is Marcus’s call, not the band’s — taken so the next stage wasn’t blocked. The band has not reviewed any of it, and it can still change.

Start with the plain-language overview if you haven’t already.

Where this sits

This is round B. It ran the same brief as round A, deliberately independently — nothing here was coordinated with that session, and where the two disagree that was treated as useful rather than as a problem.

Round B produced the single best idea in the whole exploration — the jawless cranium — and it got there because Marcus rescued a mark this session had wrongly thrown away. It also produced several conclusions the later review overturned. Both are recorded below.

Full working: brand/logo-explorations-b/ · per-round detail in each folder’s NOTES.md · the adjudication in brand/DIRECTION.md

Not artwork

Everything visual on this page is a concept for choosing a direction. The marks are raster generations and machine-traced vector; the lockups use a placeholder typeface. The final logo still has to be drawn in vector by hand. Nothing in this folder should be traced and shipped.

ROUND 0

Open the archive before generating anything

The brief said to open the 35 archive .ai files first. Doing it produced two corrections to reference/VECTOR-ASSETS.md, which had been written from byte inspection rather than from looking at the files.

  • That document calls logos/vector-source/ the “cleanest standalone masters”, with apezone_logo_Main.ai as “the leanest file, likely the tidiest construction”. Opened, apezone_logo_Main.ai is two stars on a magenta rectangle, and apezone_logo_Main_BW.ai is the ape skull, misnamed.
  • Ape_Logo2013.ai, also filed under logos, is a barcode.

Both should be fixed before anyone plans work off that document.

COLOUR

Red loses on measurement, not on taste

Three palette directions were built and an accent shoot-out run between them. Every value was authored in code (colour/palette.py) and rendered from those exact numbers — colour was never sampled out of a generated image, because generators do not honour colour specifications.

The finding on red: iron oxide #8A4A2E, the deep oxidised rust that decisions.md §6 would permit, scores 2.75:1 on every candidate ink. That fails WCAG AA and fails even the large-text threshold — so it cannot be a link, a control, or anything a reader has to see. Walked up in lightness it only passes at #C07044, by which point it is terracotta rather than rust.

Superseded — but not contradicted

Round B recommended a cold Granite base with a Sodium accent. brand/colour.md had independently settled on Aged Brass, and DIRECTION.md confirms nothing in round B reopens that. The palette in force is the one in colour.md.

What survives from round B is the reasoning, and the two sessions agreed on it independently: red loses on contrast against the ground the brand actually lives on, and the accent has to be able to do real work rather than only decorate.

ROUND 1

The skull hits a wall

First redraw pass, comparing methods. It ran straight into the problem that shaped the rest of the session: the more the skull survived being shrunk, the more it read as a generic skull-and-crossbones — which is a hard exclusion.

Text-to-vector generation was tried and abandoned here. All four unreferenced vector outputs drifted to metal and gaming iconography and lost the ape entirely. They were kept as evidence — and one of them turned out to contain the best idea in the session, so “failed as output” was not the same as “worthless”.

ROUND 2

The crest — what makes it an ape at 16 pixels

Two features turned out to carry the ape read at small sizes. This round found the first of them.

The sagittal crest — the raised ridge along the top of a gorilla’s skull. Drawn as a distinct lozenge clear of the cranium it is a simple, high-contrast silhouette event at the top of the mark, and no human skull has one. It survives every reduction. Round 2’s other answer was to delete the teeth entirely, which worked, but round 4 beat it.

ROUND 3

The 2013 lockup failed on weight, not arrangement

The historic skull-in-the-O was hairline letters against a solid red skull — the skull was the only element with any mass, so it shouted. Tested across three weights, the arrangement works at heavy weight with the skull held to cap height, and fails at light weight or at any size above cap height.

The finding that mattered most

This became a direct input to typography: the display face needs real mass. The elegant thin geometric that “grown-up” tends to default to is the wrong answer here. DIRECTION.md later turned this into a measured specification — stems at 24% of cap height, roughly double the archive’s weight.

Round 3 also established the hard limit that survived everything afterwards: the badge cannot be the favicon. No amount of craft fits seven letterspaced letters into 32 pixels, so a mark-only asset is required regardless of which arrangement wins.

ROUND 4

The jawless cranium — the session’s best outcome

How this round happened

Round 4 exists because Marcus picked a mark this session had already rejected. All four round-1 vector outputs had been dismissed on one look at a 460-pixel contact-sheet tile — and a good concept got thrown out along with its bad styling. Enlarged, one of them contained the idea that changed the recommendation.

The method lesson, recorded in round B’s own notes: enlarge before rejecting. Contact sheets rank execution; they hide ideas.

No mandible. A cranium with the lower jaw absent and two upper canines hanging free reads as a specimen, not a death’s head — which is precisely menace implied rather than announced, the thing the platform asks for. It also survives shrinking, because two thick vertical strokes are exactly the kind of shape that downsampling keeps.

Together with the crest it beat round 2’s answer measurably, not as a matter of preference — the ramp below is the evidence.

ROUND 5

Three drawings, one silhouette

Round 5 separated two failures that had been treated as one. “Soft” turned out to be a different problem from “simple” — and the favicon constraint had been over-applied to the whole identity.

Round B had been designing one mark that had to do every job from a back patch to a browser tab, which is the wrong shape for the problem. The answer was a family: three drawings sharing one silhouette, each drawn for its size range.

ROUND B’S OWN RECOMMENDATIONS

What this session concluded

Recorded as round B wrote them, before adjudication:

ItemRound B’s recommendation
ColourGranite base with a Sodium accent. Two non-red candidates pass AA comfortably; red does not.
Primary arrangementSkull alongside the wordmark, divided by a hairline. Skull in the O named a genuinely close second.
The markA three-tier family sharing one silhouette — not one drawing.
WordmarkLetterspaced capitals confirmed. Decision 1 explicitly not in question.
Do not take forwardDirection C — “safe and anonymous, and after thirty years anonymity is the one thing the band does not need to buy”.

Round B also specified what the eventual hand-drawing has to do, and that list survived adjudication essentially intact: rebuild as positive shapes with deliberate line weights (the archive skull is drawn in negative, which is why it closes up when shrunk); no mandible; crest clear of the cranium; two free-hanging canines and no other teeth; sockets level, since any inward tilt reads as angry eyebrows; no spikes, barbs or pointed flicks; compact toward square; roughly a third of the archive’s detail, and nothing thinner than a tenth of the mark’s width.

ADJUDICATION

What the review kept, and what it dropped

The design review in brand/DIRECTION.md weighed rounds A, B and C against the platform and the decisions log. Marcus accepted its recommendation on 2026-08-01 — which unblocks the next stage, but is one person’s call and is still open to the band. Round B did well out of it, and not in the places round B expected.

Round B proposedOutcome
The jawless cranium as an ideaKeptAdopted for every tier from 16 to 96px — avatar, badge, favicon. Beat round C's alternative on brand content.
A family of drawings rather than one markKeptThe tiering logic was adopted wholesale. The final system uses round B's logic with round B's drawing.
The redraw specificationKeptCarried into BUILD-SPEC.md §4. “Crest as a distinct lozenge, clear of the cranium” is called the single most important line in the spec.
Display type needs real massKeptTurned into a measured number: stems at 24% of cap height.
The r1e stencil styling as the primary markDroppedBarbed flicks and tilted sockets read as menace announced — the specific thing the platform rules out. Period tattoo-flash. The idea inside it survives; the drawing does not. This overrode Marcus's twice-confirmed pick, and the review argued it explicitly rather than quietly.
Arrangement B — skull, hairline, wordmarkDroppedJudged stock scaffolding: the layout of tech companies and esports orgs. The in-context evidence is real, but the arrangement buys genericness with the skull's legibility.
Granite / Sodium paletteDroppedAlready settled elsewhere. colour.md stands, and no round B finding reopens it.
Glyph legible at 16pxCorrected“Crest, sockets and canines legible” is true at 32px, not 16. The glyph still wins the tier — on honest numbers. At 16px it reads “tiny skull”, accepted deliberately.
The net result

The primary mark is not round B's arrangement — it is round A's letterspaced APEZONE wordmark with the skull detached, redrawn heavy. But round B's glyph carries every small size, and round B's reading of the jawless cranium is described in the review as the best single insight in three rounds.

METHOD & LIMITS

How this was made, and what it cannot tell you

  • 24 generations used, inside a 30 budget. The saving came from dropping text-to-vector early and building the lockup work in code instead.
  • Generation was reference-guided throughout, anchored on the real Skull.ai parsed out of the archive.
  • Colour was never sampled from a generated image. Every value authored in colour/palette.py and rendered from those numbers.
  • The traced SVGs are tracing under-layers, not masters. At 9–21 paths they carry two to three times the nodes a hand-drawn version needs, with the lumpy tangents tracing always leaves. A head start, nothing more.
  • Nothing was seen on paper, at physical size, or on a real phone. Every size claim is a render at nominal pixel sizes — a good proxy, not the thing. The 16px favicon decision in particular still owes a check in an actual browser tab.
  • The lockups use a placeholder typeface. The real display face is task 2.3.

Left open by round B: typography (2.3) untouched beyond the weight finding; a light-mode paper variant; and whether the crossbarless chevron Λ inherited from the 2013 wordmark is worth keeping. That last one was later answered — the chevron stays, overturning round A's advice to correct it.
